confirmedRules.name: Only managers and admins may approve or reject tasks
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Approving or rejecting a task that is pending approval is restricted to users whose role is ADMIN or MANAGER. MEMBER and VIEWER users are refused.
confirmedRules.given: User 'dev' with role MEMBER is logged in and task #3 is PENDING_APPROVAL
confirmedRules.when: dev posts action=approve for task 3
confirmedRules.then: The request is refused with HTTP 403 and task 3 stays PENDING_APPROVAL. If user 'mgr' (MANAGER) does the same, task 3 becomes DONE
confirmedRules.parameters: Approver roles = {ADMIN, MANAGER}. The check is enforced twice: AuthFilter.java:40-47 (403 'Only managers or admins may approve or reject tasks') and TaskActionServlet.java:91-98 (403 'Approval requires a manager or admin').
edgeCases: Gated actions are only 'approve' and 'reject'. start, submit, reopen and bulkClose have no role gate
A missing session user is treated as not authorized (403) by TaskActionServlet. In practice AuthFilter redirects to /login first
The submitter can approve their own task if they are a MANAGER/ADMIN. There is no segregation-of-duties check
The approver role is read from the session snapshot taken at login, so a role change in the DB does not apply until the user logs in again
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should a manager be allowed to approve a task they are assigned to or submitted themselves (no segregation-of-duties check exists today)? | Should a VIEWER be allowed to start, submit or reopen tasks, and should an approver be barred from approving their own submitted task?

confirmedRules.name: New tasks start OPEN and editing never changes status
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Every new task starts in status OPEN. Editing a task changes its title, description, priority, assignee and due date, but never its status. Status changes only happen through the transition actions.
confirmedRules.given: Task #2 is IN_PROGRESS
confirmedRules.when: The user edits task 2, changing priority from HIGH to LOW and saving
confirmedRules.then: Task 2 keeps status IN_PROGRESS, its priority becomes LOW, and updated_at is refreshed
confirmedRules.parameters: Initial status = OPEN (TaskStatus.OPEN). The update SQL at TaskDao.java:97-112 excludes the status and project_id columns.
edgeCases: Project reassignment: the form sends projectId, but TaskDao.update does not write project_id, so changing a task's project on edit is silently ignored
Editing a non-existent id updates 0 rows but still redirects with saved=1
Editing a DONE task is allowed (no lock on completed tasks)
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The edit form lets the user pick a different project and validates it, but the update SQL never persists project_id, so the change is silently lost. | The edit form lets the user pick a different project, but the update never saves it. A user can believe they moved a task to another project when they did not.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should users be able to move a task to another project on edit (the UI offers it but the change is never saved)? Should DONE tasks be editable? | Should a task be movable to another project after it is created? The UI suggests yes, but the save logic ignores the change.

confirmedRules.name: Task list filtering by status and assignee
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The task list shows every task, optionally narrowed by status and/or assignee. When both filters are given, a task must match both.
confirmedRules.given: Seed data with 4 tasks, 3 assigned to person 3 and one IN_PROGRESS
confirmedRules.when: /tasks?status=IN_PROGRESS&assignee=3 is requested
confirmedRules.then: Only 'Wire up SSO' is returned
confirmedRules.parameters: Filters: t.status = ? (when non-empty), t.assignee_id = ? (when present). Combined with AND. Wiring at TaskListServlet.java:22-37. The API uses the status filter only (ApiTaskServlet.java:24-27).
edgeCases: An empty status means all statuses
There is no 'unassigned' filter: unassigned tasks can only be seen with no assignee filter
An unknown status value returns an empty list (no validation)
A non-numeric assignee raises a 500
There is no visibility restriction: every logged-in user sees every task in every project, archived ones included

confirmedRules.name: Project lifecycle: create as ACTIVE, archive one way
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A new project needs a non-blank name, starts ACTIVE, and is owned by the user who created it. An ACTIVE project can be archived. Archived projects cannot be reactivated.
confirmedRules.given: User 'mgr' (id 2) submits project name '  Zephyr  '
confirmedRules.when: The create form is posted, and later action=archive is posted for that project
confirmedRules.then: Project 'Zephyr' is created ACTIVE with owner 2. After archiving, its state is ARCHIVED. Archiving it again changes nothing (0 rows)
confirmedRules.parameters: Initial state = 'ACTIVE'. Archive SQL: UPDATE project SET state='ARCHIVED' WHERE id=? AND state='ACTIVE'. States allowed by schema.sql:22-23 = ACTIVE, ARCHIVED. Name validation and owner assignment at ProjectServlet.java:31-51 (HTTP 400 'Project name is required').
edgeCases: There is no role check on create or archive: any logged-in user, VIEWER included, can do both
Archiving has no effect on the project's tasks, and new tasks can still be added to it
There is no un-archive path in the code
projects.jsp:32 links to /projects/delete, but no servlet is mapped for it in web.xml, so delete is not implemented
The project name is trimmed. The description is optional and not trimmed (DB max 1024)
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Who is allowed to create and archive projects (today anyone, including VIEWER)? Should archiving freeze the project's tasks, and is project deletion a required feature?

confirmedRules.name: User roles and what VIEWER can actually do
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: There are four user roles: ADMIN, MANAGER, MEMBER and VIEWER. The only permission that differs between them in code is approve/reject (ADMIN, MANAGER).
confirmedRules.given: User 'view' has role VIEWER
confirmedRules.when: view creates a task, starts it, submits it, bulk-closes tasks, or archives a project
confirmedRules.then: All of these succeed. Only approve/reject are refused (403)
confirmedRules.parameters: Roles: ADMIN, MANAGER, MEMBER, VIEWER (also a DB CHECK at schema.sql:14-15).
edgeCases: ADMIN and MANAGER have identical permissions in code
MEMBER and VIEWER have identical permissions in code
An unknown role string in the DB would make Role.valueOf throw during login or the people list (PersonDao.java:51)
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The role name VIEWER suggests read-only access, but nothing enforces it. Viewers can create, edit, transition, bulk-close tasks and archive projects.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: What is VIEWER intended to be allowed to do? Should it be read-only, and should MEMBER be restricted (e.g., only start/submit tasks assigned to them)?

confirmedRules.name: Task data domain constraints
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Every task must have a title of up to 256 characters, a status from the four lifecycle values, a priority of LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH, and a valid project. The assignee and due date are optional but must reference a real person and be a calendar date.
confirmedRules.given: An insert with priority 'URGENT'
confirmedRules.when: The task is saved
confirmedRules.then: The database rejects it with a CHECK violation, which the app shows as a 500 error
confirmedRules.parameters: title VARCHAR(256) NOT NULL; description VARCHAR(4000); status IN (OPEN, IN_PROGRESS, PENDING_APPROVAL, DONE) default OPEN; priority IN (LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH) default MEDIUM; project_id NOT NULL FK project; assignee_id nullable FK person; due_date DATE nullable. Person: username VARCHAR(64) unique; full_name VARCHAR(128); role CHECK. Project: name VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL; description VARCHAR(1024).
edgeCases: Project names are not required to be unique
There is no cascade on delete, so a person or project referenced by tasks cannot be deleted
No constraint stops a due date from being in the past

confirmedRules.name: Bulk close marks selected tasks DONE, bypassing the approval workflow
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A user can select several tasks and close them at once; every selected task that is not already DONE is set straight to DONE regardless of its current status or the user's role.
confirmedRules.given: A logged-in VIEWER selects task #3 (OPEN), #4 (PENDING_APPROVAL) and #5 (DONE)
confirmedRules.when: They submit action=bulkClose with ids=3,4,5
confirmedRules.then: Tasks #3 and #4 become DONE with refreshed updated_at; #5 is unchanged (already DONE); the user is redirected to the task list. No role or status check is applied.
confirmedRules.parameters: SQL: UPDATE task SET status='DONE' WHERE status <> 'DONE' AND id IN (...). Entry point TaskActionServlet.java:76-88. Empty or missing ids -> silent redirect, no change.
edgeCases: Empty selection -> no-op redirect to /tasks
Already-DONE tasks are skipped so their updated_at is not touched
Non-existent ids are silently ignored
Non-numeric id -> NumberFormatException (500)
AuthFilter's approver check only looks at action=approve/reject, so bulkClose is open to every role
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Bulk close lets any role (including MEMBER and VIEWER) take OPEN or PENDING_APPROVAL tasks straight to DONE, which gets around the rule that only managers and admins can approve. The class comment says 'each action checks the task's current status', but bulk close does not. | Bulk close goes around the approval workflow. Any role, including VIEWER, can take OPEN, IN_PROGRESS or PENDING_APPROVAL tasks straight to DONE without manager or admin approval. This contradicts the README rule that only ADMIN/MANAGER may approve. | Bulk close bypasses both the lifecycle guard and the approver-role check. Any logged-in user, VIEWER included, can move OPEN/IN_PROGRESS/PENDING_APPROVAL tasks straight to DONE, which defeats the manager-approval policy. The class comment (TaskActionServlet.java:13-17) says each action checks the expected status, but bulk close does not.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is bulk close meant to be an admin/manager-only override, and should it only apply to tasks in particular statuses (for example PENDING_APPROVAL)? | Is bulk close meant to let any user, including MEMBER and VIEWER, mark tasks DONE without approval? Or should it be limited to approvers, or to tasks that are already PENDING_APPROVAL? | Is bulk close meant as an approver-only administrative override, or should it close only PENDING_APPROVAL tasks and require ADMIN/MANAGER like approve does?

confirmedRules.name: Login required for the application, with plaintext credential match
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Every page needs a logged-in user except the login page, stylesheets, and anything under /api/. A user logs in when the username and password exactly match a stored person record.
confirmedRules.given: An anonymous visitor with no session
confirmedRules.when: They request /tasks
confirmedRules.then: They are redirected to /login. After posting a matching username and password they get a session holding their Person (id, name, role) and are redirected to /tasks; a wrong pair shows 'Invalid credentials' on the login page.
confirmedRules.parameters: Exempt paths: /login, /api/*, *.css. Credential check: PersonDao.java:16-29 (SELECT ... WHERE username=? AND password=?, plaintext). Session attribute 'user'. Logout (LogoutServlet.java:12-18) invalidates the session and redirects to /login. Seed passwords: <credential - masked, see src/main/resources/db/seed.sql:2-6>.
edgeCases: /api/tasks (ApiTaskServlet.java:23-27) is reachable without login and returns every task, or those with ?status=X, as JSON
Any path ending in .css skips authentication
Passwords are stored and compared in plaintext; there is no lockout or attempt limit
Username match is exact (case-sensitive by DB default); usernames are unique (schema.sql:11)
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The /api/ exemption means the whole task list (titles, statuses, assignees, due dates) can be read without logging in. Passwords are stored in plaintext. | The /api/ exemption exposes every task (titles, assignees, statuses, due dates) to unauthenticated callers through ApiTaskServlet (ApiTaskServlet.java:22-49). Passwords are stored and compared in plaintext (PersonDao.java:17-18).
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is /api/tasks meant to be public, or is it only meant for internal callers such as the read-only oracle checks? | Is /api/tasks intentionally public (e.g., for an internal integration), or should it require authentication like the UI?

confirmedRules.name: New-task defaults and what an edit may change
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A new task always starts OPEN with MEDIUM priority unless another priority is chosen, and assignee and due date are optional. Editing a task updates its title, description, priority, assignee and due date but never its status.
confirmedRules.given: A user creates a task 'Write docs' in project 2 with no priority, no assignee and no due date
confirmedRules.when: The form is saved
confirmedRules.then: The task is stored with status OPEN, priority MEDIUM, no assignee and no due date, and the user lands on its detail page (/tasks/form?id=N&saved=1). If they later edit it to priority HIGH while it is IN_PROGRESS, it stays IN_PROGRESS and updated_at is refreshed.
confirmedRules.parameters: Default status OPEN (TaskFormServlet.java:66); default priority 'MEDIUM' (line 58; also DB default schema.sql:34). Update SQL TaskDao.java:97-112 sets title, description, priority, assignee_id, due_date, updated_at=CURRENT_TIMESTAMP. Every status or field write refreshes updated_at.
edgeCases: Any submitted status value is ignored on create; it is always OPEN
An empty assignee means unassigned (NULL)
On edit, project_id is validated but never written, so the project chosen on the form is silently ignored
Editing a DONE task is allowed and does not change its status
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: On edit, the form checks the chosen project exists but TaskDao.update never writes project_id, so moving a task to another project silently does nothing.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should a task be movable between projects, and should DONE tasks be locked against editing?

confirmedRules.name: Task list filtering and sort order
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The task list can be filtered by status and/or assignee and sorted by a fixed set of options. By default the most recently updated tasks come first, and priority sorting uses business order HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW.
confirmedRules.given: Tasks A (LOW, updated 10:00), B (HIGH, updated 09:00), C (MEDIUM, updated 11:00)
confirmedRules.when: The list is requested with sort=priority
confirmedRules.then: The order is B, C, A; with no sort parameter the order is C, A, B (updated_at descending).
confirmedRules.parameters: Sort tokens: updated (default) -> updated_at DESC; status -> status, updated_at DESC; priority -> HIGH=0, MEDIUM=1, other=2, then updated_at DESC; due or due_date -> due_date, updated_at DESC; title -> title, id; id -> id. Filters: TaskDao.search (TaskDao.java:40-56) combines status and assignee with AND; TaskListServlet.java:31-32.
edgeCases: Unrecognized sort tokens fall back to updated_at DESC
Tasks with no due date sort last under the PostgreSQL default (NULLS LAST ascending)
Filtering for unassigned tasks is not possible (a null assignee means no filter)
Non-numeric assignee parameter -> NumberFormatException (500)

confirmedRules.name: Task status lifecycle (guarded state machine)
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A task moves OPEN -> IN_PROGRESS -> PENDING_APPROVAL -> DONE, can be rejected from PENDING_APPROVAL back to IN_PROGRESS, and reopened from DONE to OPEN. Each action is refused unless the task is currently in the one status that action expects.
confirmedRules.given: Task #7 is in status IN_PROGRESS
confirmedRules.when: a user posts action=start (which expects OPEN)
confirmedRules.then: the change is refused with HTTP 409 'Cannot start a task in status IN_PROGRESS (expected OPEN)' and the status stays IN_PROGRESS. Posting action=submit instead moves it to PENDING_APPROVAL and refreshes updated_at.
confirmedRules.parameters: Transitions: start OPEN->IN_PROGRESS; submit IN_PROGRESS->PENDING_APPROVAL; approve PENDING_APPROVAL->DONE; reject PENDING_APPROVAL->IN_PROGRESS; reopen DONE->OPEN. Guard: TaskActionServlet.java:101-109 (HTTP 409 on mismatch). Unknown action -> HTTP 400; unknown task id -> HTTP 404. After success, redirect to /tasks, or to the task detail page when return=detail.
edgeCases: There is no direct OPEN->DONE, IN_PROGRESS->DONE or PENDING_APPROVAL->OPEN action. The only way around this is bulk close (separate rule).
Reopen goes all the way back to OPEN, not IN_PROGRESS.
approve/reject check the user's role before the status, so a MEMBER approving a task that is not pending gets 403, not 409.
The check reads and then writes with no lock or conditional UPDATE (TaskDao.updateStatus has no 'AND status = expected'), so two concurrent actions can both pass the guard.
The UI only shows the buttons that are valid for the current status (tasks.jsp:57-69, task-form.jsp:46-58), but the server guard is what actually enforces it.
LifecycleTest.java:27-39 (testDirectOpenToDone) calls the DAO directly to go OPEN->DONE. The test bypasses the servlet guards, so it does not test the business rule.
A request with no id and an action other than bulkClose fails when it parses the id (HTTP 500), before the 400 check for an unknown action.
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The guard and the write are not atomic: TaskDao.updateStatus (TaskDao.java:115-125) writes the status without checking the current status, so a race can apply a transition from the wrong state. | The status precondition is not part of the UPDATE (no 'AND status = expected'), so concurrent requests can race past the guard; any code path that calls TaskDao.updateStatus directly bypasses the lifecycle entirely.

confirmedRules.name: Every task change refreshes its last-updated timestamp
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Any edit or status change to a task sets its updated_at to the current database time, and that timestamp drives the default 'recently updated' ordering.
confirmedRules.given: task #1 last updated 2026-07-15 09:00:00 and listed last by default
confirmedRules.when: a user starts task #1 at 2026-11-02 10:30:00
confirmedRules.then: its updated_at becomes 2026-11-02 10:30:00 and it moves to the top of the default task list.
confirmedRules.parameters: updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP in update (line 99), updateStatus (line 118) and bulkClose (line 136). Insert uses the schema default CURRENT_TIMESTAMP (schema.sql:39). Shown truncated to whole seconds (TaskDao.java:234-236).
edgeCases: Bulk close does not refresh tasks that are already DONE (they are excluded by the WHERE clause).
A form save with no actual changes still refreshes the timestamp.

confirmedRules.name: Project lifecycle: ACTIVE to ARCHIVED, forward only
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A project can be archived only while it is ACTIVE. Archiving is one-way: nothing restores a project, and archiving an already-archived project does nothing.
confirmedRules.given: project Borealis (id 2) is ACTIVE
confirmedRules.when: any signed-in user posts action=archive for id 2 to /projects
confirmedRules.then: its state becomes ARCHIVED. Repeating the request changes nothing and returns no error.
confirmedRules.parameters: UPDATE project SET state='ARCHIVED' WHERE id=? AND state='ACTIVE'. Servlet: ProjectServlet.java:33-37. The Archive button shows only for ACTIVE projects (projects.jsp:25-31).
edgeCases: No role check: MEMBER and VIEWER can archive any project, not only the owner.
Archiving does not change the project's tasks. They keep their statuses and stay fully actionable.
New tasks can still be created in an ARCHIVED project (TaskFormServlet only checks that the project exists).
projects.jsp:32 shows a 'Delete' link to /projects/delete, but web.xml maps no servlet to that path, so deletion is not a real capability.
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Archived projects still accept new tasks and task transitions, so 'archived' carries no business meaning beyond a label. Any user, including VIEWER, can archive any project.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: What should archiving a project prevent: new tasks, edits or transitions on its tasks? And who may archive (owner, MANAGER/ADMIN only)? | Who may archive a project (owner, managers, admins), and what should happen to open tasks in an archived project?

confirmedRules.name: Project creation defaults
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A new project needs a non-blank name (leading and trailing spaces are trimmed). It is created ACTIVE and owned by the user who created it.
confirmedRules.given: signed-in user 'mgr' (id 2)
confirmedRules.when: they create a project named '  Zephyr  ' with no description
confirmedRules.then: project 'Zephyr' is created in state ACTIVE with owner_id 2. A blank name is refused with HTTP 400 'Project name is required'.
confirmedRules.parameters: Initial state ACTIVE (ProjectDao.java:58, schema.sql:22). Owner = session user. Name max 128 characters (schema).
edgeCases: Any role, including VIEWER, can create projects.
Duplicate project names are allowed (no unique constraint).
The description is not trimmed.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should project creation be limited to certain roles (for example ADMIN/MANAGER), and must project names be unique?

confirmedRules.name: Task save validation
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A task cannot be saved without a non-blank title and a project that exists. Priority defaults to MEDIUM and the assignee and due date are optional.
confirmedRules.given: a user submits the task form with title '   ' and project 1
confirmedRules.when: the form is posted
confirmedRules.then: nothing is saved and the form is shown again with 'Title is required'. With title 'Fix login' and project 999 (no such project) the error is 'A task must belong to an existing project'.
confirmedRules.parameters: Title trimmed; max 256 characters (schema). Default priority MEDIUM (line 58). Assignee empty -> unassigned (null). Due date ISO yyyy-MM-dd or empty -> null.
edgeCases: An ARCHIVED project passes the existence check.
A priority outside LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH is only caught by the database CHECK constraint (server error, not a friendly message).
A badly formed due date or a non-numeric projectId/assigneeId causes a server error.
A user who does not exist as assignee is only caught by the foreign key.
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Tasks can be created in or moved into ARCHIVED projects, because the existence check ignores project state.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should creating or moving tasks into an ARCHIVED project be blocked? | Should new tasks be allowed in ARCHIVED projects, and should due dates in the past be rejected?

confirmedRules.name: Allowed values for status, priority, role and project state
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The database is the authority on allowed values: task status (OPEN, IN_PROGRESS, PENDING_APPROVAL, DONE), task priority (LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH), person role (ADMIN, MANAGER, MEMBER, VIEWER) and project state (ACTIVE, ARCHIVED).
confirmedRules.given: any code path writes a task with status 'CANCELLED'
confirmedRules.when: the row is inserted or updated
confirmedRules.then: the database rejects the write with a CHECK constraint violation.
confirmedRules.parameters: task.status default OPEN; task.priority default MEDIUM; project.state default ACTIVE (schema.sql:22-23); person.role CHECK (schema.sql:14-15). Status strings are also repeated in TaskStatus.java and Role.java.
edgeCases: The values are duplicated in Java constants and the JSP dropdowns, so changing one place will not update the others.
The list and API status filters accept any text without checking it; an unknown status just returns an empty list.

confirmedRules.name: Access policy: approve/reject is the only role-restricted action
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Every page needs a signed-in user except the login page, stylesheets and the /api/ JSON feed. Apart from approve/reject, any signed-in user, including VIEWER, can create, edit, transition, bulk close and archive.
confirmedRules.given: user 'view' with role VIEWER is signed in
confirmedRules.when: they post action=start on an OPEN task, or edit a task's title
confirmedRules.then: the change goes through. Only action=approve or action=reject gets HTTP 403.
confirmedRules.parameters: Public paths: /login, /api/*, *.css. Unauthenticated users are redirected to /login.
edgeCases: GET /api/tasks returns every task (title, status, assignee, project, due date) with no authentication.
The VIEWER role is not read-only in practice, despite its name.
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: VIEWER has the same write access as MEMBER, and the /api/tasks feed is unauthenticated.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should VIEWER be read-only (no create, edit, transitions, bulk close or archive)? Should MEMBER be allowed to reopen DONE tasks? Is /api/tasks meant to be public?

confirmedRules.name: Sign-in by username and password
confirmedRules.source: src/main/java/com/acme/tracker/web/LoginServlet.java:23-35 (session creation, redirect to /tasks, 'Invalid credentials' error) together with src/main/java/com/acme/tracker/dao/PersonDao.java:16-29,46-53 (plaintext username/password match and role mapping)
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A user signs in when the username and password exactly match a stored person. The person and their role are then kept in the session for later permission checks.
confirmedRules.given: a stored person 'mgr' with role MANAGER
confirmedRules.when: they sign in with the matching password
confirmedRules.then: a session is created holding the user, including role MANAGER, and they are sent to /tasks. A wrong password shows 'Invalid credentials'.
confirmedRules.parameters: Passwords are stored and compared as plain text. Seed passwords: <credential - masked, see src/main/resources/db/seed.sql:2-5> (preview 'ad****'; each seed password equals its username). A read-only reporting DB role is also created with a hardcoded password: <credential - masked, see src/main/resources/db/oracle-ro.sql:8> (preview 'or****').
edgeCases: The role is cached in the session at sign-in, so a role change does not apply until the user signs in again.
No lockout or retry limit.
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Plaintext password storage and comparison. Seed and DB-role passwords are hardcoded.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Citation was corrected by referee (The behavior is real, but the cited lines cover only part of it. PersonDao.java:16-29 does the credential match: line 18 runs a parameterized query `SELECT id, username, full_name, role FROM person WHERE username = ? AND password = ?`, and lines 21-22 bind the username and password as given, as plain text with no hashing. The comment at line 17 says the same thing and is harmless. It returns the mapped Person, with role from Role.valueOf at line 51, when a row matches, or null when none does (line 24). The rest of the Given/When/Then is not in the cited range. It is in LoginServlet.java:23-35, which calls people.authenticate(...) at line 27. If the result is null, lines 29-30 set the error 'Invalid credentials' and forward back to /WEB-INF/jsp/login.jsp. On success, line 33 creates the session and stores the user, role included, as attribute "user", and line 34 redirects to contextPath + "/tasks". The Parameters claims check out. In seed.sql:2-5 each seed password equals its username (preview 'ad****', 'mg****'). oracle-ro.sql:8 creates the role oracle_ro with a hardcoded password (preview 'or****'). One caveat: 'exactly match' relies on SQL `=`, so case sensitivity depends on the database collation and is not enforced in the Java code. The cited region contains no instruction-shaped text.) — confirm src/main/java/com/acme/tracker/web/LoginServlet.java:23-35 (session creation, redirect to /tasks, 'Invalid credentials' error) together with src/main/java/com/acme/tracker/dao/PersonDao.java:16-29,46-53 (plaintext username/password match and role mapping) is the authoritative implementation.

confirmedRules.name: Task list ordering options
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: By default the task list shows the most recently updated tasks first. Users can sort by status, priority (HIGH before MEDIUM before LOW), due date, title or id, with recency as the tie-breaker.
confirmedRules.given: tasks with priorities LOW, HIGH and MEDIUM
confirmedRules.when: the list is requested with sort=priority
confirmedRules.then: they appear HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, and equal priorities appear newest first.
confirmedRules.parameters: Tokens: updated (default), status, priority, due/due_date, title, id. Anything else falls back to updated_at DESC.
edgeCases: Status sorts alphabetically (DONE, IN_PROGRESS, OPEN, PENDING_APPROVAL), not in lifecycle order.
Any priority value other than HIGH or MEDIUM sorts as LOW.
Tasks with no due date sort last (PostgreSQL ascending default).
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should the status sort follow lifecycle order (OPEN, IN_PROGRESS, PENDING_APPROVAL, DONE) rather than alphabetical?

confirmedRules.name: Task timestamps shown to whole seconds; due dates as ISO dates
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A task's last-updated time is truncated (not rounded) to whole seconds, as yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss. Its due date is a plain yyyy-MM-dd date with no time part.
confirmedRules.given: A task whose updated_at in the database is 2026-07-17 14:23:05.987
confirmedRules.when: The task is read for the list, the detail page or the JSON API
confirmedRules.then: updatedAt is "2026-07-17 14:23:05" (the first 19 characters of the timestamp text; the .987 is dropped, not rounded up to :06)
confirmedRules.parameters: Truncation length 19 characters. Due date format yyyy-MM-dd (java.sql.Date.toString).
edgeCases: A timestamp on an exact second ("...:05.0") becomes "...:05".
A null updated_at gives null, though the schema makes the column NOT NULL.
Sorting uses the full-precision database value, so two tasks showing the same second can still have a fixed order between them.

confirmedRules.name: Due date is optional, must be an ISO date, and has no range check
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A task may have no due date. If one is given it must be a yyyy-MM-dd date. Any past or future date is accepted, and the system never works out whether a task is overdue.
confirmedRules.given: A user saves a task with due date "2026-06-10", which is before today's date of 2026-11-02
confirmedRules.when: The task is created or edited
confirmedRules.then: The due date 2026-06-10 is stored without warning. A blank due date stores no due date. A value such as "10/06/2026" fails parsing with an unhandled error (HTTP 500), not a form error message.
confirmedRules.parameters: Parser: java.sql.Date.valueOf (yyyy-[m]m-[d]d). Blank means NULL.
edgeCases: A blank field clears an existing due date when editing.
Single-digit months and days ("2026-6-5") are probably accepted.
Out-of-range days within 1-31 (for example "2026-02-30") probably roll over to a real date (2026-03-02) instead of being rejected.
No overdue flag, reminder or due-date check exists anywhere in the code.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should the rewrite reject impossible dates (such as Feb 30) and past due dates with a user-facing message, or keep the legacy behavior of accepting any parseable date and failing hard on bad formats?
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: A due date in the wrong format causes a server error instead of a form validation message.

confirmedRules.name: Editing a task cannot move it to another project
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Editing a task can change its title, description, priority, assignee and due date, but not its project. A different project chosen on the edit form is silently ignored.
confirmedRules.given: Task #1 belongs to project Apollo (id 1)
confirmedRules.when: A user edits task #1, selects project Borealis (id 2) and saves
confirmedRules.then: The task stays in Apollo. The page still shows "Saved." because the UPDATE statement never writes project_id.
confirmedRules.parameters: Columns updated on edit: title, description, priority, assignee_id, due_date, updated_at. Not updated: project_id, status.
edgeCases: The edit form still requires a project that exists (TaskFormServlet.java:50-53), even though the value is then discarded.
Editing an id that does not exist updates 0 rows, but the user is still sent to the 'Saved.' page (TaskFormServlet.java:68-74).
An empty description saves as an empty string, not NULL.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should a task be movable between projects? The edit form offers a project picker, but the save logic ignores it. Is that an intended lock or a bug?
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The edit form shows an editable project dropdown and reports success, but the project change is never saved.

confirmedRules.name: Tasks may be created in archived projects
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The only project check on a task save is that the project exists. Archived projects appear in the task form's project list and accept new tasks, and archiving a project does nothing to its tasks.
confirmedRules.given: Project 'Legacy Archive' (id 3) has state ARCHIVED
confirmedRules.when: A user creates a task with projectId=3
confirmedRules.then: The task is created as OPEN in the archived project. Existing tasks in archived projects can still be started, submitted, approved and reopened.
confirmedRules.parameters: exists() runs SELECT 1 FROM project WHERE id = ?, with no filter on state. The form's project list is ProjectDao.findAll(), which includes ARCHIVED projects, ordered by name (lines 19-31).
edgeCases: Archiving (ProjectServlet.java:33-37) does not close, freeze or reassign the project's tasks.
A non-numeric projectId fails with an unhandled NumberFormatException.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should archived projects be closed to new tasks and task status changes, or is archiving only a label? | When a project is archived, should its open tasks be closed, blocked, or hidden, and should new tasks be refused in archived projects? Who may archive a project: only its owner, managers/admins, or anyone? | Should creating or moving a task into an ARCHIVED project be blocked, and should archived projects be hidden from the task form's project list?
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: 'Archived' has no effect on work in the project. Users can keep adding tasks to a project described as decommissioned. | Archiving has no business effect on tasks, and it is not authorized beyond being signed in. | Archiving a project does not freeze its tasks. New tasks can be created in an ARCHIVED project, and existing ones edited or moved there.

confirmedRules.name: Signing out ends the session
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Signing out ends the user's session and returns them to the login page. No explicit session expiry is set.
confirmedRules.given: Logged-in user Morgan Manager
confirmedRules.when: Morgan opens /logout
confirmedRules.then: The session is invalidated and Morgan is redirected to /login. Later pages need a new login.
confirmedRules.parameters: No <session-config> timeout in web.xml, so the servlet container's default applies.
edgeCases: Logout without a session still redirects to /login.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: What idle timeout should sessions have? The legacy app relies on the container default. | Is there a required idle-timeout or maximum session length for this internal tool, and must a role change take effect immediately for active sessions?

confirmedRules.name: Any user of any role can be assigned a task
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The assignee list contains every person sorted by full name, whatever their role, and the server only checks that the assignee id is a known person (through the foreign key), so read-only VIEWERs can be given work.
confirmedRules.given: Person 4 'Vic Viewer' has role VIEWER
confirmedRules.when: A task is saved with assigneeId=4
confirmedRules.then: The task is saved as assigned to Vic Viewer; leaving assigneeId empty saves it as unassigned (shown as '(unassigned)')
confirmedRules.parameters: People list: SELECT ... FROM person ORDER BY full_name, with no role filter. Shown by task-form.jsp:88-93. The assignee is parsed at TaskFormServlet.java:60-61, and the FK fk_task_assignee is at schema.sql:41.
edgeCases: An assigneeId that does not exist fails the FK and returns a 500, not a friendly message
An assigneeId that is not a number throws NumberFormatException (500)
A VIEWER assigned a task cannot be stopped from starting or submitting it, since only approve/reject check the role
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should VIEWER-role users (and possibly ADMINs) be excluded from the assignee list, and should a bad assignee give a validation message rather than a server error? | Should read-only VIEWER accounts be assignable as task owners?

confirmedRules.name: Status guards exist only in the web layer; the data layer accepts any status jump
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The raw status update writes any status to any task without checking where it starts from, and the test suite checks that a task can go straight from OPEN to DONE. The approval workflow is enforced only by the TaskActionServlet checks.
confirmedRules.given: A new task 'Spike: caching layer' in status OPEN, priority LOW, project 1
confirmedRules.when: TaskDao.updateStatus(id, 'DONE') is called directly
confirmedRules.then: The task is DONE with no IN_PROGRESS or PENDING_APPROVAL step and no approver check, and the test passes
confirmedRules.parameters: Raw write is TaskDao.updateStatus (TaskDao.java:114-125, 'Raw status write'). testNormalFlow (LifecycleTest.java:41-55) also drives OPEN, IN_PROGRESS, PENDING_APPROVAL, DONE without an approver identity.
edgeCases: Anything that calls the DAO directly (batch jobs, future APIs, tests) skips the 409 guard and the manager/admin rule
Bulk close is a second DAO path that skips the guards
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The test treats skipping approval as expected behaviour. A rewrite that moves the guards into the domain layer would fail testDirectOpenToDone. | The test suite codifies the approval bypass as expected behavior. A rewrite that uses these tests as its specification would keep a path to DONE that never goes through approval. | The regression baseline encodes an approval bypass as correct behavior, and the check-then-write guard lets concurrent approve/reject requests conflict.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is the direct OPEN to DONE path in testDirectOpenToDone a real allowed transition (e.g. for admins), or should the domain layer reject it? | Is moving a task from OPEN (or IN_PROGRESS) straight to DONE without manager approval ever allowed, for example for spikes or admin clean-up? If so, who may do it? Or should the rewrite enforce the approval workflow at the domain/data level and treat testDirectOpenToDone as recording a defect? | Should the rewrite's tests keep 'direct OPEN to DONE' as valid behavior, or replace it with a test that this jump is rejected outside bulk close?

confirmedRules.name: Order of checks for a single-task action
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A single-task action runs these checks in order: the user must be signed in, the task must exist (else 404), approve/reject need a manager or admin (else 403), the task must be in the expected status (else 409), and the action must be known (else 400). On success the user returns to the task list, or to the task detail page if return=detail.
confirmedRules.given: A signed-in MEMBER
confirmedRules.when: They post action=approve for task id 999 that does not exist
confirmedRules.then: AuthFilter blocks the request with 403 'Only managers or admins may approve or reject tasks' before any lookup. A MANAGER posting the same request gets 404 'No such task'.
confirmedRules.parameters: Existence check at TaskActionServlet.java:31-36, role check in AuthFilter.java:42-49 and again at TaskActionServlet.java:49/54, status guard 409 at :100-109, unknown action 400 at :62-64, redirect target at :66-73 ('/tasks' by default, '/tasks/form?id=<id>' when return=detail).
edgeCases: A missing or non-numeric id parameter throws NumberFormatException (500), not 400
An unknown action on an existing task gives 400 'Unknown action: <action>'
A missing action parameter is treated as '' and gives 400 'Unknown action: null'

confirmedRules.name: Bulk close: empty selection is ignored and no role is required
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Bulk close with no tasks ticked does nothing and returns to the list. Otherwise any signed-in user, VIEWER included, can close the selected tasks, so PENDING_APPROVAL tasks can be completed without a manager.
confirmedRules.given: A VIEWER is signed in and task 3 'Migrate invoices' is PENDING_APPROVAL
confirmedRules.when: They tick task 3 and press 'Close selected (bulk)'
confirmedRules.then: Task 3 becomes DONE with a fresh updated_at and the user is sent back to /tasks. With nothing ticked the redirect happens and no task changes.
confirmedRules.parameters: No role check in handleBulkClose. AuthFilter only restricts action=approve/reject (AuthFilter.java:42-49). The UI form is tasks.jsp:38-78.
edgeCases: A non-numeric id in ids throws NumberFormatException (500) and no tasks close
The user is not told how many tasks were closed; the bulkClose return value is ignored
Tasks already DONE are left alone by the DAO filter
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: A VIEWER or MEMBER can use bulk close to bypass the manager/admin approval rule.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should bulk close be limited to managers/admins, or limited to tasks that are not PENDING_APPROVAL, for users who cannot approve?

confirmedRules.name: Unauthenticated JSON read-back of tasks with optional status filter
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: GET /api/tasks returns every task as JSON with id, title, status, priority, assigneeId, projectId, dueDate and updatedAt (no description), newest-updated first. An optional status parameter limits the list to that exact status.
confirmedRules.given: The seeded data and no session
confirmedRules.when: A client calls GET /api/tasks?status=DONE
confirmedRules.then: It receives [{"id":4,"title":"Archive old data","status":"DONE","priority":"LOW","assigneeId":1,"projectId":2,"dueDate":null,"updatedAt":"2026-07-15 18:00:00"}]
confirmedRules.parameters: The auth exemption for /api/* is in AuthFilter.java:28-33. The filter uses an exact status match. Ordering is updated_at DESC (TaskDao.findAll at :22-24, or search with the default sort). Timestamps are cut to 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss' (TaskDao.java:234-236).
edgeCases: status=done (lowercase) or an unknown status returns [] rather than an error
An empty status parameter returns all tasks
There is no assignee or project filter and no paging
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Anyone who can reach the endpoint can read the whole task list, including assignment and due dates, without signing in. | The hand-written JSON escaping does not escape control characters, so a task title with a line break breaks the JSON for every consumer.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is /api/tasks meant to be public (e.g. for a dashboard or integration), or should it require authentication or a service token? | Is unauthenticated access to the task API intended (e.g. for an integration partner or monitor)? If so, which consumers rely on the exact field set and ordering?

confirmedRules.name: Transition buttons offered depend only on current status, not on the user's role
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Each task shows only the actions valid from its status: OPEN shows Start, IN_PROGRESS shows Submit for approval, PENDING_APPROVAL shows Approve and Reject, DONE shows Reopen. Approve/Reject are shown to every role even though only managers and admins can use them.
confirmedRules.given: A MEMBER views task 3 in PENDING_APPROVAL
confirmedRules.when: The task list or detail page is shown
confirmedRules.then: Approve and Reject buttons are visible, and clicking either returns 403
confirmedRules.parameters: The same per-status logic is on the detail page (task-form.jsp:42-59), which posts return=detail.
edgeCases: A VIEWER sees Start, Submit and Reopen and can use them because they have no role check
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should the UI hide Approve/Reject (and possibly every transition) for roles not allowed to use them?

confirmedRules.name: Archive offered only for active projects; Delete link has no backing function
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The projects page shows Archive only for ACTIVE projects, but shows a Delete link for every project. That link goes to /projects/delete, which has no servlet mapping, so projects can never be deleted.
confirmedRules.given: Project 1 'Apollo' is ACTIVE and project 3 'Legacy Archive' is ARCHIVED
confirmedRules.when: Any signed-in user views /projects
confirmedRules.then: Apollo shows Archive and Delete, Legacy Archive shows only Delete, and clicking Delete returns 404
confirmedRules.parameters: The archive post is handled with no role or owner check at ProjectServlet.java:32-37. The servlet mappings in web.xml:71-78 cover only /projects.
edgeCases: A forged archive post for an already ARCHIVED or unknown id changes nothing (DAO filter) and still redirects without telling the user
Any role, VIEWER included, can archive any project, not only the owner
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The Delete link points to an endpoint that does not exist. Archive has no ownership or role check. | Dead UI action: the Delete link has no backing endpoint. | The UI offers a Delete action with no server-side handler.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is project deletion a required feature, and if so what happens to its tasks? Should archiving be limited to the project owner or managers/admins? | Should projects be deletable at all? If so, what happens to their tasks (block, cascade, or reassign) and which roles may delete? Or should the Delete link be removed in the rewrite? | Is project deletion a required feature that was never built, or should the rewrite drop the Delete link and keep projects permanently, archive-only?

confirmedRules.name: Status-change precondition: refuse unless the task is in the expected status (check-then-write, not atomic)
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Every single-task status action first reads the task's current status and refuses with a conflict if it is not the status that action requires; but the later write does not re-check the status, so two people acting at the same moment can both succeed.
confirmedRules.given: Task #3 is PENDING_APPROVAL and a manager presses Approve while another manager presses Reject on the same page
confirmedRules.when: Both requests read the status PENDING_APPROVAL before either one writes
confirmedRules.then: Both pass the guard. The task ends up DONE or IN_PROGRESS depending on which write lands last. A request that reads a different status gets HTTP 409 with the message 'Cannot <action> a task in status <current> (expected <expected>)'
confirmedRules.parameters: Rejection outcome: HTTP 409 CONFLICT. The response text names the current and expected status. Missing task id gives HTTP 404 'No such task' (TaskActionServlet.java:31-36). The write is TaskDao.updateStatus (TaskDao.java:115-125): UPDATE ... WHERE id = ? with no status condition
edgeCases: A request with an unknown or missing action gets HTTP 400 'Unknown action: <action>' (TaskActionServlet.java:62-64), and this check runs only after the task lookup
After a successful transition the user goes to the task list. With return=detail they go back to that task's detail page instead (TaskActionServlet.java:66-73)
A non-numeric id throws NumberFormatException, which the user sees as a server error, not a validation message
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Time-of-check/time-of-use race: the guard and the UPDATE are separate steps and the UPDATE has no 'AND status = expected' clause. Two concurrent approve/reject (or approve/reopen) requests can both apply, and the final state depends on timing. The rewrite should make the transition a single conditional update and report failure when 0 rows change.

confirmedRules.name: Initial data: one account per role and tasks seeded in every lifecycle state
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Every fresh database starts with four sign-ins, one for each role, whose passwords equal their usernames, plus three projects (two active, one archived) and four tasks, one in each status.
confirmedRules.given: A fresh deployment (the in-memory DB is re-seeded on every start)
confirmedRules.when: Someone signs in as the seeded manager
confirmedRules.then: They authenticate with the default password. Seeded state: tasks 1 OPEN, 2 IN_PROGRESS, 3 PENDING_APPROVAL, 4 DONE; project 3 'Legacy Archive' ARCHIVED
confirmedRules.parameters: Seeded users: admin/ADMIN, mgr/MANAGER, dev/MEMBER, view/VIEWER. Passwords: <credential — masked, see seed.sql:3-6, preview 'ad**'> (each equals its username). Project owners: Apollo -> person 2, Borealis and Legacy Archive -> person 1
edgeCases: The seed hard-codes ids 1..4, and the rest of the seed relies on IDENTITY assigning them in that order
Seeded passwords are stored in plaintext in person.password
The README (README.md:76) publishes the default sign-ins
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Is the seed reference data that production must also have (e.g. a mandatory admin account), or demo/test data only? Must default credentials be forced to change on first login? | Are these seed accounts loaded in production, and must the rewrite force a password change or remove them? | Is seed.sql loaded in production, or only in demo/test environments?
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Shipped default accounts use password = username, stored in plaintext. | The default accounts, including ADMIN, ship with guessable plaintext passwords. | Known default credentials, including ADMIN, are stored in plaintext in every deployment that loads the seed.

confirmedRules.name: Read-only reporting access to all tables, including plaintext passwords
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A separate database login with read-only rights is created for reporting and verification. It can read every table, including the person table with its plaintext passwords, but cannot change data.
confirmedRules.given: The oracle_ro database login
confirmedRules.when: It queries SELECT username, password FROM person
confirmedRules.then: The query succeeds and returns every user's plaintext password. Any INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE is denied
confirmedRules.parameters: Role: oracle_ro, LOGIN, password <credential — masked, see oracle-ro.sql:8, preview 'or**'>. Grants: CONNECT on database tracker, USAGE on schema public, SELECT on all current tables, and default SELECT on future tables
edgeCases: The default privileges mean new tables are readable automatically
The role is recreated on every fresh database start (deploy configmap line 81 has an identical copy)
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Which reporting consumers use the read-only login, and should it be allowed to see the person table (credentials) at all? | Should the read-only role be allowed to read the person table's password column?
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The read-only role can read the credential column, and its own password equals its name.

dataObjects.name: Task (model bean)

fields.name: id
fields.note: PK; read from task.id (TaskDao.java:222); set from the id request param on edit (TaskFormServlet.java:69-70)

fields.name: title
fields.note: Required. Servlet trims it and rejects an empty value (TaskFormServlet.java:41,45-47), matching NOT NULL VARCHAR(256) (schema.sql:30). The servlet does not check the 256-char length.

fields.name: description
fields.note: Optional free text, taken from the request as-is (TaskFormServlet.java:57); VARCHAR(4000) (schema.sql:31)

fields.name: status
fields.note: Plain String, not an enum. Comment lists the values (Task.java:7); constants in TaskStatus. Always set to OPEN on create (TaskFormServlet.java:66); not in the UPDATE column list (TaskDao.java:98), so an edit never changes it. Changed only by updateStatus (TaskDao.java:115-125) and bulkClose (TaskDao.java:128-147)

fields.name: priority
fields.note: LOW|MEDIUM|HIGH by comment (Task.java:8). Defaults to MEDIUM when blank (TaskFormServlet.java:58). The servlet does no whitelist check; only the DB CHECK enforces it (schema.sql:34-35), and a bad value surfaces as a RuntimeException

fields.name: assigneeId
fields.note: Optional FK to person (schema.sql:36,41). Never filtered by role: any person from PersonDao.findAll can be picked (task-form.jsp:90-93). Null is read back via rs.wasNull (TaskDao.java:227-228)

fields.name: assigneeName
fields.note: Display only, from LEFT JOIN person (TaskDao.java:17,20,229)

fields.name: projectId
fields.note: Required. The servlet only checks that the project exists (TaskFormServlet.java:50; ProjectDao.exists ProjectDao.java:45-55), not that it is ACTIVE, so archived projects accept new tasks. Written on INSERT (TaskDao.java:85) but left out of the UPDATE (TaskDao.java:98-99), so on edit it is silently ignored even though the servlet sets it (TaskFormServlet.java:59)

fields.name: dueDate
fields.note: Comment Task.java:13. Blank is stored as NULL. Otherwise it goes through java.sql.Date.valueOf (TaskDao.java:182-187), which throws IllegalArgumentException on a bad format. That exception is not caught as SQLException, so the user gets an unhandled 500. No range check. Read back via Date.toString (TaskDao.java:232-233)

fields.name: updatedAt
fields.note: Timestamp cut to whole seconds with substring(0,19) (TaskDao.java:234-236). Set to CURRENT_TIMESTAMP on update, updateStatus and bulkClose (TaskDao.java:99,118,136). On INSERT the column is omitted and the DB default applies (schema.sql:39)
